conventions: Both verbless cola are read predicate-first as the ASV construes them: the copula joins נַחֲלַת (*are a heritage*) and שָׂכָר (*is reward*), with בָּנִים and פְּרִי הַבָּטֶן as subjects, on the strength of the chiastic parallel (children ∥ fruit of the womb; heritage ∥ reward). The competing reading, which rule 49's definite-construct-chain sentence would suggest, puts *are* on בָּנִים as the indefinite predicate; it was considered and not taken.
report: Checked all ten candidate lemmas: every difference is licensed by context. הַ unrepresented only in the title (no *the* written); suffix הוּא as *it*/*his*/unrepresented by function (objective genitive on the participle, possessive, second reference to the house under rule 22); בְּ unrepresented only in בּוֹ where the ASV drops the phrase (rule 40); יהוה takes *of* only as a rectum; לְ *of*/*for*/*unto* as written; שָׁוְא *in vain* as adverbial accusative (127:1 twice) and *is vain* as verbless predicate (127:2); אֵת object marker vs preposition H854; בָּנָה and שָׁמַר finite vs substantival participle; כֵּן bare *so* beside a verb (127:2) and *So are* as verbless predicate (127:4), which matches the corpus's 14 *so is* units.

Read the dump end to end for `added` consistency: supplied possessives with no suffix (127:3 *his*, 127:5 *their*) both added; supplied connectives for asyndetic cola (127:2 *For*, 127:3 *And*) both added; 127:1 restrictive *but* and 127:2 anticipatory *It* added on their own terms. No split hidden from the lemma table.
127:1 fuses אִם לֹא → *Except* in both cola, headed on the negative, discontinuous across the subject (rules 30, 35); consistent within the verse and the note names the competing head.

127:3 places the copula on נַחֲלַת (*are a heritage*) and on שָׂכָר (*is reward*), reading both cola predicate-first as the ASV does and as the chiastic parallel (children ∥ fruit of the womb; heritage ∥ reward) supports. Rule 49's sentence that a definite construct chain is the subject would put *are* on בָּנִים instead; that reading is defensible but not preferable, so the accepted alignment stands — recorded as a convention so a later reader does not relitigate it.

BSB disagreements (127:1 בּ and וֹ of בּוֹ): convention, not error. The ASV renders the house once as the object *it* of *build*, which the objective-genitive suffix on בוֹנָיו carries; בּוֹ is left with nothing under rules 40 and 22. Not a genuine error.
The repeated note 'Rectum takes *of* (rule 19)' restates the contract and needs no convention. Nothing here generalises; no promotions or amendments.
